human_semantics_review: Six distinct side-edge spans visible at native 768px. Red/green/blue source spans end at the original gray water surfaces; B depth sides use the declared swapped identities. All I/II/III and A-E labels legible. Water and footprint fills unchanged. No new contour or water level is drawn. Human can ignore the pairing and use the unchanged identities and volume/height ordering.

per_marker_review.role: Front vase 1 left side below the original water surface: actual water-height span, not a new level.
Front vase 2 left side below the original water surface: actual water-height span, not a new level.
Front vase 3 left side below the original water surface: actual water-height span, not a new level.
B top view vase 1 depth edge: color-paired to source vase 3, swapping I/III while keeping II.
B top view vase 2 depth edge: color-paired to source vase 2, swapping I/III while keeping II.
B top view vase 3 depth edge: color-paired to source vase 1, swapping I/III while keeping II.

primary_math_review: All three front widths are equal. A rectangular vase volume is front width times depth times water height. Water heights satisfy hII>hI>hIII. Because VI=VIII=4, depthIII>depthI. Also VII=3<4 and hII>hI, so depthII<depthI. Hence depthIII>depthI>depthII. Only A has that depth ordering. B reverses I and III; C,D,E fail the necessary ordering. Relative pixel heights are not treated as exact givens.
